headline: Mirza Fakhrul takes oath as 23rd president of Bangladesh
summary: The veteran BNP leader was elected in the country's first contested presidential race since 1991, defeating the Jamaat-e-Islami-led alliance candidate.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sworn in as the 23rd President of Bangladesh at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban on Friday evening. Speaker-in-charge Barrister Kayser Kamal administered the oath.
Fakhrul was elected on Thursday with 255 votes, defeating Col (retd) Oli Ahmed, the candidate of the Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance, who received 88 votes.
This marks the country's first contested presidential election since 1991. Fakhrul, a veteran BNP leader and former secretary general, resigned from his party post on August 13 to run for the office.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman attended the ceremony and later wished the new president a successful and dignified tenure via Facebook, emphasizing a commitment to democracy and constitutional dignity.
The event was attended by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, former chief adviser Prof Muhammad Yunus, Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman, and various political leaders and diplomats.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is now the 23rd President of Bangladesh, winning the first contested presidential race since 1991.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sworn in as the 23rd President of Bangladesh at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban on Friday evening. Speaker-in-charge Barrister Kayser Kamal administered the oath.

Fakhrul was elected on Thursday with 255 votes, defeating Col (retd) Oli Ahmed, the candidate of the Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance, who received 88 votes.

This marks the country's first contested presidential election since 1991. Fakhrul, a veteran BNP leader and former secretary general, resigned from his party post on August 13 to run for the office.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman attended the ceremony and later wished the new president a successful and dignified tenure via Facebook, emphasizing a commitment to democracy and constitutional dignity.

The event was attended by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, former chief adviser Prof Muhammad Yunus, Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman, and various political leaders and diplomats.

headline: 6 new members join Tarique-led cabinet in reshuffle
summary: Four ministers and two state ministers have taken oath at Bangabhaban, with portfolios assigned by the Cabinet Division gazette.
details: Six new members, comprising four ministers and two state ministers, have officially taken oath at Bangabhaban to join the BNP-led government's cabinet.

According to the Cabinet Division gazette, portfolios have been assigned to these new members. Moin Khan has been appointed to the Ministry of Local Government, while Partha has been assigned to the Information Ministry.
Other key appointments include Millat in the Aviation and Tourism ministry and Saching Pru in the Chittagong Hill Tracts ministry.
Additionally, Afroza Khanam has been named as the Food Minister, and Zahir Uddin Swapan has been appointed as an advisor to the Prime Minister.
This reshuffle marks the first major adjustment to the cabinet portfolios under the current administration's leadership.
caption:
6 new members join the cabinet! Portfolios have been assigned for the first major reshuffle.

Six new members, comprising four ministers and two state ministers, have officially taken oath at Bangabhaban to join the BNP-led government's cabinet.

According to the Cabinet Division gazette, portfolios have been assigned to these new members. Moin Khan has been appointed to the Ministry of Local Government, while Partha has been assigned to the Information Ministry.

Other key appointments include Millat in the Aviation and Tourism ministry and Saching Pru in the Chittagong Hill Tracts ministry.

Additionally, Afroza Khanam has been named as the Food Minister, and Zahir Uddin Swapan has been appointed as an advisor to the Prime Minister.

This reshuffle marks the first major adjustment to the cabinet portfolios under the current administration's leadership.
